name: Gemini CLI

surfaces.label: gemini launched by npm, Homebrew or MacPorts (node running the bin symlink)

node run directly on the bundle path (npx cache, source checkout, npm layout where argv[1] is the real script). Note: the relaunch child inherits the parent argv[1], so on a symlinked install it matches the first surface, not this one
standalone single-executable binary (release asset gemini-darwin-<arch>-unsigned.zip contains the file gemini; the relaunch child is also named gemini)

gemini --acp: Agent Client Protocol server over stdio, spawned by an editor (Zed and other ACP clients). Needs a gemini needle because other node agents (for example the qwen-code fork) also take --acp
gemini --experimental-acp: the deprecated spelling of the same ACP server. Separate surface because args_contain is substring AND and '--acp' is not a substring of '--experimental-acp'

working_signals.meaning: Bursty. A record is appended when the user prompt is accepted, when a model response completes, and when tool calls finish. Nothing is written while a response is streaming or a long tool runs, so a stale file does not mean idle.
Inferred, not measured. The Ink UI redraws its spinner and streamed text during a turn; idle is expected near 0 percent. Not observed on a real instance.

waiting_signals.meaning: Fires with notification_type ToolPermission when a tool call needs approval. Observability only. The docs list ToolPermission as the only type.

OSC 0 title starts with the hand icon and 'Action Required' while a confirmation is pending. Dynamic titles: '◇  Ready' idle, '✦  <thought or Working…>' mid-turn, '⏲  Working…' when silent for a while. Read from the terminal emulator, not from ps. Hidden by ui.hideWindowTitle, and folder-only when ui.dynamicWindowTitle is false.
Opt-in (general.enableNotifications). OSC 9 or terminal bell on 'action required' and 'session complete'. Terminal-side only, no file or process trace.

hooks.config: hooks object in ~/.gemini/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json, or system /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/settings.json (override with GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH); also shipped by extensions. Toggle with hooksConfig.enabled.

telemetry.how: Off by default. GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true (or telemetry.enabled in settings.json). Target local or gcp, OTLP grpc or http, default endpoint http://localhost:4317, GEMINI_TELEMETRY_OUTFILE for a file. Logs, metrics and traces (traces need GEMINI_TELEMETRY_TRACES_ENABLED). Events include gemini_cli.user_prompt, gemini_cli.tool_call, gemini_cli.api_request, gemini_cli.agent.start and gemini_cli.agent.finish.

sources.evidence: package.json in google-gemini/gemini-cli at fe63502: "bin": {"gemini": "bundle/gemini.js"}; https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula/gemini-cli.json printed versions.stable 0.46.0, dependencies ['node']; npm dist-tags latest 0.61.0, preview 0.62.0-preview.0, nightly 0.63.0-nightly.20260929; the formula is deprecated true (date 2026-06-18, reason unsupported, replacement cask antigravity-cli, disable_date 2026-12-18)

sources.claim: the launcher re-executes itself as a child process (process.execPath) with GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH=true, so a session appears as two nested processes (node+node, or gemini+gemini for the standalone binary). The child argv is [...process.execArgv, memory flag if needed, process.argv[1], ...args], so it repeats the parent's script path. The supervisor is skipped when GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH or SANDBOX is set
sources.evidence: packages/cli/index.ts run() lines 54-131 (spawn(process.execPath, spawnArgs, {stdio: inherit+ipc}) inside `if (!GEMINI_CLI_NO_RELAUNCH && !SANDBOX)`) and packages/cli/src/utils/processUtils.ts getSpawnConfig lines 107-160. Corrected in verification: the earlier cite of relaunch.ts relaunchAppInChildProcess was wrong, that function has no call site (grep of packages/cli and packages/core). index.ts is unchanged in tag v0.61.0

sources.claim: no macOS bundle id: Gemini CLI has no desktop app in the repo; the only GUI-adjacent package is a VS Code companion extension (publisher google), not a separate agent process
sources.evidence: packages/ lists a2a-server, cli, core, devtools, sdk, test-utils, vscode-ide-companion; no Info.plist or bundle id anywhere in the tree

sources.claim: flags that carry a session id: --session-id <uuid> (new session with given id) and --resume/-r (value is 'latest', an index, or an id); the three session flags are mutually exclusive
sources.evidence: packages/cli/src/config/config.ts lines 242-248 (sessionFlags mutual exclusion) and options 'resume' (line 401, alias r), 'session-file', 'session-id' (line 426), present at main and v0.61.0. https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/cli-reference/ documents --resume/-r only; --session-id and --acp are source-only, the doc lists --experimental-acp

sources.claim: a plain 'gemini' launch has no session id in argv, so a process cannot be mapped to its transcript by argv alone; the fallback is cwd -> project slug (~/.gemini/projects.json) -> newest chats file
sources.evidence: packages/core/src/config/storage.ts (projects.json under the global runtime dir, project dir tmp/<slug>) and packages/core/src/config/projectRegistry.ts getShortId. Fallback is inferred, not observed.

sources.claim: transcripts are JSONL at ~/.gemini/tmp/<project-slug>/chats/session-<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm>-<first 8 chars of session id>.jsonl; first line is metadata (sessionId, projectHash, startTime, lastUpdated, kind, directories), then one message record per line, plus {"$set":{...}} update lines; legacy .json files are migrated to .jsonl on resume; subagent transcripts nest under chats/<parent session id>/<id>.jsonl
sources.evidence: packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts initialize() and appendRecord(); packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingTypes.ts (SESSION_FILE_PREFIX='session-', ConversationRecord, MessageRecord types user|info|error|warning|gemini). Same jsonl code present at tags v0.46.0 and v0.61.0

sources.claim: docs state sessions live in ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/ (docs never name the file format or file names; the hook reference calls the transcript JSON)
sources.evidence: https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/session-management/ (docs/cli/session-management.md). The code now uses a slug from projects.json rather than a hash; the docs wording is stale

sources.evidence: packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts lines 547, 565, 1652 (recordMessage), 1636/1641 (queued thoughts and tokens, flushed with the message), 1715 (recordToolCalls)

Gemini CLI is being retired for consumers: from 2026-06-18 it stops serving Google AI Pro/Ultra and free Code Assist for individuals users, who are moved to Antigravity CLI (binary agy, Go). Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise and paid API key use continues. Antigravity CLI is a different product and needs its own row

notes: Gemini CLI is sunset for consumer accounts since 2026-06-18 (see sources), so many Macs will run Antigravity CLI (agy) instead; this row only covers the Gemini CLI. Never run against a live instance. (1) Session start is two nested node processes; the probe keeps the outermost, which is why tool_children is left out of working_signals: the inner node and any MCP stdio servers are always children, so 'has non-caffeinate children' would read as working forever. (2) Session mapping is weak: the id is in argv only for --session-id or --resume <uuid>; the transcript file name carries just the first 8 characters of the id, so per_session needs a {session_id_first8} substitution the current probe does not do. (3) Docs say <project_hash>; current code uses a slug. Glob with a wildcard. (4) The best real turn signal is the terminal title, which needs the terminal emulator, not ps. Settings can hide it. (5) headless -p runs are matched too and are simply working for their lifetime. (6) False-positive risk, unfixable with substring args_contain: 'bin/gemini' also matches any node process with an argument such as .../node_modules/.bin/gemini-mcp or /usr/local/bin/gemini-anything, and the bare name 'gemini' matches any unrelated executable called gemini (a Gemini-protocol client, for example). Not tested on a live process list. (7) On npm/Homebrew installs both the supervisor and the child match the first surface (same argv[1]); the probe keeps the outer one. (8) session_id_args '--resume'/'-r' often carry 'latest' or an index, not an id, and bare --resume is followed by nothing or a prompt, so the probe can read a wrong id. (9) The Homebrew formula is deprecated (disable date 2026-12-18) and pinned at 0.46.0.
